:::{#exr-matmul-assoc-practice}
#### Grouping a product of three matrices

By @thm-matmul-assoc, a [product](#def-matrix-mult) of three [matrices](#def-matrix) can be grouped either way,
so $\matr{A}\matr{B}\vx$ can be computed as $\matr{A}(\matr{B}\vx)$,
without ever forming $\matr{A}\matr{B}$.
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\vx = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix},
$$

where $\vx$ is a $2 \times 1$ matrix.

Find $\matr{A}\matr{B}\vx$ by computing $\matr{B}\vx$ first.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

By @def-matrix-mult, $\matr{B}\vx$ is a $2 \times 1$ [matrix](#def-matrix);
multiply $\matr{A}$ by it.

:::
